extracted.intended_audience: high-school creative writing students and instructors at an arts conservatory
extracted.subtask_description: A high-school level assessment rubric for creative writing pieces (typically short stories or narrative prose) used to score student work on multiple craft dimensions using a 1–4 scale. Designed for classroom evaluation and formative feedback in an arts-conservatory setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique premise, fresh ideas, surprising angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories typically scored 1–4 (Beginning / Developing / Proficient / Exemplary). Assesses whether the piece offers an original concept, unexpected perspective, or imaginative details that set it apart. Exemplary work presents fresh premises or surprising twists and avoids clichés; lower scores indicate derivative material, predictable outcomes, or reliance on stock ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice / Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive narrative voice, intentional tone, control of register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the author's control of voice and stylistic choices: consistent and appropriate tone, distinct narrator/character voice, syntactic variety, and purposeful register. Exemplary pieces demonstrate a confident, original voice that enhances meaning; weaker pieces show inconsistent tone, inappropriate register, or flat/invisible narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Language / Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise diction, vivid imagery, figurative language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on exactness and vividness of language: strong verbs, concrete nouns, evocative imagery, and apt figurative language. High scores reflect precise, sensory language that clarifies character and scene; low scores show vague wording, reliance on modifiers, cliché metaphors, or awkward phrasing that obscures meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure / Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear narrative arc, intentional pacing, scene structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges overall organization and pacing: effective beginning/middle/end, scene sequencing, transitions, and momentum. Exemplary submissions have purposeful structure that supports theme and emotional payoff; poor structure includes disjointed scenes, weak pacing, confusing chronology, or lack of clear narrative trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-dimensional characters with motivation and arc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses depth and growth of characters: clear desires, believable motivations, complexity, and change (arc) where appropriate. Strong work renders characters with inner life revealed through action and dialogue; weak work relies on flat or stereotypical figures, unexplained behavior, or lack of development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting & Atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how well setting and atmosphere are rendered to create place and mood: sensory detail, specificity of time/place, and how setting supports theme and character. Exemplary pieces integrate setting organically; lower scores use generic or sketchy backdrops that fail to establish mood or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict & Theme
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates the central conflict(s) — stakes, clarity, and integration with theme — and whether the piece achieves thematic depth without being didactic. High scores show conflicts that drive character choices and yield resonant thematic conclusions; low scores lack clear stakes, present irrelevant obstacles, or state themes overtly without complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conventions / Mechanics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers technical correctness and presentation: grammar, punctuation (including dialogue punctuation), spelling, paragraphing, and adherence to submission formatting. Exemplary submissions are clean and polished; mechanical errors that distract from reading will lower scores and suggest insufficient proofreading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafts demonstrate considered editing and growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the submission shows signs of revision: tightened prose, structural changes, clarified imagery, or improved characterization compared to earlier drafts. High scores indicate deliberate editing choices that strengthen the piece; absence of revision evidence suggests work may be first-draft quality or unrefined.
